Compare models fitted to the same data

Source: R/loo.R
compare_models.Rd

One row per fit: its model, whether it passes diagnose(), its approximate leave-one-out score from loo(), and, if given, its crossval() scores. All fits must be made to the same observed cells (the same data, whatever the formula, spatial prior or nugget).

Usage

compare_models(..., cv = NULL, loo = NULL)

Arguments

...

Two or more fit_areal() objects, named (e.g. compare_models(leroux = fit1, bym2 = fit2)); unnamed ones are named by their expressions.

cv

Optional: crossval() results, a list named as the fits, with the same folds and seed for every model (see compare_cv()).

loo

Optional: loo() results already computed, a list named as the fits (any fit left out is computed here).

Value

A data frame, best first (by elpd_loo): model, spatial (the spatial prior and any fixed hyperparameters), nugget, n_hyper (free hyperparameters), n_beta (fixed effects), pass (diagnose()), elpd_loo, se_elpd_loo, elpd_diff, se_diff, p_loo, n_k_high (cells with a high Pareto k, see loo()); and with cv: cv_log_score, cv_diff, cv_se_diff, cv_pct_outside_95, cv_rmse. The loo results are attached as attribute loo.

Details

Scores are expected log predictive densities: higher is better. elpd_diff is each model's difference from the best (0 for the best, negative for the others), summed over cells, and se_diff its standard error from the cell-by-cell differences, as in loo::loo_compare(). A difference smaller than about two standard errors is not a clear preference. The cross-validation columns are per cell (cv_log_score is the mean log score of compare_cv()), as there.

Why not AIC, BIC or DIC: AIC needs a number of parameters, which a model with a latent value per cell does not have (the effective number, p_loo here, depends on the hyperparameters); BIC approximates a marginal likelihood that, in a hierarchical model, is driven by the priors; and DIC is unreliable for latent Gaussian models. Predictive scores avoid all three problems.

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_areal(areal_lattice(4, 4), time_frame(n_steps = 5), n_cells = 40, seed = 1)
ctl <- list(n_iter = 200, n_burn = 100, n_store = 50, n_chains = 2, n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
compare_models(leroux = fit_areal(sim, control = ctl),
               bym2 = fit_areal(sim, spatial = "bym2", control = ctl),
               no_nugget = fit_areal(sim, nugget = FALSE, control = ctl))
#>       model spatial nugget n_hyper n_beta  pass  elpd_loo se_elpd_loo
#> 1      bym2    bym2   TRUE       4      2 FALSE -125.4016    4.186919
#> 2    leroux  leroux   TRUE       4      2 FALSE -126.1897    3.992879
#> 3 no_nugget  leroux  FALSE       3      2 FALSE -126.5311    4.311237
#>    elpd_diff  se_diff    p_loo n_k_high
#> 1  0.0000000 0.000000 4.134368        4
#> 2 -0.7880569 1.502263 4.249251        8
#> 3 -1.1295210 1.500586 6.349915       10
# }
